about: The releases of the Compassionism Simulation’s findings, newest first. Written by dev/tools/release_data.py; see dev/ADDING-A-RELEASE.md.

releases.summary: v5.9 leads both pages, with a central-bank switch. The simulation page opens on v5.9’s main row (full backing, the design’s statement), for the full-coverage design or the opt-in design, with the central bank off (the frozen model, registered on OSF without a central bank, 500 seeds) or on (a policy-rate rule, the central-bank study, 100 seeds). The central-bank study’s runs were repeated with the release’s global settings, which its first runs had left out (preregistration Amendment 4), and the findings page shows every outcome of the corrected study. The v5.6 panel is unchanged (v5.6’s data stays the data shown in its sections), and the engine is unchanged.

The v5.9 release, whose main results are the frozen model (engine 104691f, preregistered and frozen before it ran on Nov 14, 2026, registered on OSF, first published as v5.8), beside v5.6. The v5.6 panel is unchanged (v5.6’s data stays the data shown above), and the engine’s code is the same as v5.7’s: the new model’s switches (asset classes and the creditor side, the weighted top tail, the price rule, the backing mechanism, the financed rows, the distribution measures) are in the engine behind switches, off unless a study turns them on. What 5.8 adds is the findings page’s section on the new model and its six data files in data/studies/ (r2-effects, r2-curves, r2-backing, r2-financed, r2-distribution, r2-work), with the 24 charts: the main effects of both designs in three environments at 20 and 40 years, every preregistered reading of each outcome, the backing curve with the model’s own mechanism and the break-even share, the financed rows (shown, never led with), who gains, and work. The unfavourable results are shown with the same prominence as the headline.

No change to any headline figure: the merged published panel of the full study batch (engine ce8d030) equals v5.6’s panel in all 47,466 values, so v5.6’s data stays the data shown on this page. What 5.7 adds is the data of the preregistered studies behind their switches (the no-programme baseline against outside data, the synergy of the design’s parts, the community layer, participation, open access to community-owned providers, the full-coverage design’s coverage and adequacy, the cost-of-living line) in data/studies/, and the frozen panel of the full-coverage design.

Today’s safety net in every run: SNAP (with its work rule for adults without children under 14), the earned income tax credit and the refundable Child Tax Credit are paid in the no-program run and beside Compassionism, so the program is measured against today’s US policy; SNAP’s income limit is no longer read as a tax on all earnings.

No engine change: every figure is identical to 5.4’s, so the 5.4 data stays the data shown on this page. What 5.5 adds is the 500-seed study of which settings the results are most sensitive to (the study page).

Labor and markets: people lose jobs and find new ones (with unemployment insurance, and lower pay after a permanent loss), community housing keeps its own books, community businesses cut prices sector by sector and members can leave, and new measures of risk: how far savings fall, how fast income recovers, how often people fall back into poverty.

Households and children: adults live in households as US adults do, children bring a quarter of the adult allowance, households pool their money, start with the wealth the Federal Reserve’s survey shows and spend less when income is short; and what each part of the design does is measured.
The model round: savings that keep up with prices, ageing, the no-programme run against US data, a middle backing reading and robustness readings, each beside an unchanged main result.
Audit fixes: the wage-bonus test reads this year's BU spending, the price level as a typical run with a range, the Hub's own targets beside the results, and the backing-share curve.
The external audit pass on v5.0: text, tests and page fixes, with the 40-year horizon added; the 20-year figures are v5.0's.
The first release of the release engine: Compassionism as specified on the Hub, every mechanism in, against no programme, in three environments over 20 years.
